name: addpipe24_ks_vectorized
rationale: Our earlier per-bit-generate Kogge-Stone (attempt_001) already matched baseline WNS almost exactly (7.51732 vs 7.51866) but cost +19 area units (549.822 vs 530.936), suggesting the tool's native '+' mapping realizes the same logical (KS-like) depth/speed but with a more area-efficient gate network -- likely because our per-bit named generate signals created many small individually-named wires that inhibited cross-stage sharing/rebalancing during synthesis. This candidate expresses the exact same mathematically-identical Kogge-Stone recurrence using whole-vector shift/mask bitwise operations (g,p as 24-bit vectors combined via <<, &, | per stage) instead of per-bit generate assigns. This is a much more regular, compact RTL description that should let Yosys's word-level optimizer treat each stage as a single shift-and-mask operation, exposing more opportunities for logic sharing/rebalancing similar to what happens internally for the native '+' operator, while preserving the identical logical function (and therefore the same near-baseline critical path) as the already-validated per-bit KS. Goal: retain ~7.51 WNS while closing some/all of the area gap versus the 530.936 baseline, ideally landing on or above the current best proxy-reward point.
